title: Seeing with sound: The role of echocardiography in cardiac care

body_markdown:
### For patients facing heart disease, answers often begin with sound. Heart disease remains the leading cause of death, and for patients, echocardiography, also called echo or cardiac ultrasound, can provide a glimpse into heart function. The technology uses sound waves to create moving images of the heart, helping care teams see how the heart is pumping, how blood is flowing and whether valves or heart muscles are showing signs of disease.


These images can help physicians evaluate heart function, identify possible damage, better understand symptoms such as chest pain or shortness of breath and guide decisions about follow-up care or treatment. Behind each image is a cardiac sonographer whose skill, precision and compassion help turn complex technology into meaningful insights for patients and their physicians.


A cardiologist is only as good as the sonographer. If we don’t obtain those images, we end up missing the diagnosis.


For more than 25 years, Jeff Hill has made cardiac care his world. He began his career caring directly for patients as a cardiac sonographer and now helps prepare the next generation as an assistant professor and director of echocardiography.


Throughout his professional journey, Jeff has seen how echocardiography can support care decisions. In some cases, echocardiography may help identify signs of disease for the first time. In others, it may help clinicians monitor a known condition, assess changes in heart function or inform follow-up care decisions.


That combination of technology and human expertise is what has kept Jeff inspired. While imaging technology has become more advanced over the years, he believes the person behind the probe remains central to the patient experience.


As a professor, Jeff teaches students to pair technical excellence with empathy, recognizing that many patients arrive for an echo feeling uncertain, anxious or afraid. His goal is to help future sonographers understand that every image they capture is connected to a person waiting for answers.


As echo continues to play an important role in evaluating and managing heart disease, Jeff’s work helps support a field that remains focused on both imaging expertise and the patient experience.


*Disclosure:* Jeff Hill is a paid consultant to Lantheus.


Every human deserves great compassion. They don’t want to be in that hospital or clinic. They’re scared, and your job is to make them feel as comfortable as possible.
